title: 11. SSH Brute-Force Log Detection (Cyber Security Sim)
description:
Given a list of Linux authentication log lines strings in the standard format:
`'Oct 10 14:32:10 server sshd[1234]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 192.168.1.50 port 44210 ssh2'`
or
`'Oct 10 14:32:15 server sshd[1235]: Accepted password for root from 192.168.1.10 port 44212 ssh2'`

Write a function `detect_brute_force(logs: list[str], threshold: int) -> list[str]` that extracts all unique IP addresses that generated `>= threshold` 'Failed password' attempts.

Return the list of malicious IPs sorted in alphabetical order.
constraints:
• 0 <= len(logs) <= 10^4
• 1 <= threshold <= 100
• Optimal Time: O(N) | Optimal Space: O(IPs)

logs: Oct 10 14:32:10 server sshd[123]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 192.168.1.50 port 44210 ssh2
Oct 10 14:32:11 server sshd[124]: Failed password for invalid user root from 192.168.1.50 port 44211 ssh2
Oct 10 14:32:12 server sshd[125]: Failed password for invalid user test from 192.168.1.50 port 44212 ssh2
Oct 10 14:32:15 server sshd[126]: Accepted password for root from 192.168.1.10 port 44213 ssh2
Oct 10 14:00:01 srv sshd[1]: Failed password for root from 10.0.0.1 port 22
Oct 10 14:00:02 srv sshd[2]: Failed password for root from 10.0.0.2 port 22
Oct 10 14:00:03 srv sshd[3]: Failed password for root from 10.0.0.1 port 22
Oct 10 14:00:04 srv sshd[4]: Failed password for root from 10.0.0.2 port 22

explanation: Compiled regular expression extracts IPv4 addresses directly following 'Failed password ... from'. A `Counter` aggregates failure frequency per IP. Any IP meeting the threshold is returned in sorted order, matching real-world SIEM intrusion detection heuristics.
